chats.answer:
For a Bambu Lab P1S, I recommend a pure sine wave UPS rated for at least 1000W, preferably 1500W or more, if you want to keep printing through power flickers and short outages.

The important distinction is:

Power flickers (milliseconds to seconds): A conventional UPS is ideal. It switches to battery fast enough to prevent the printer from rebooting.

Short outages (5–30 minutes): A larger UPS can work, depending on battery capacity and whether the heated bed is running.

Long outages (30 minutes to hours): A portable power station with UPS functionality and a large battery is generally more practical.

The P1S can draw roughly 1,000W or more briefly when heating its bed and nozzle on 120V power, but its consumption is much lower during typical printing. Your backup needs to handle both the peak load and the total energy consumed.

Best options for a P1S

1500VA / 1000W pure sine wave UPS. Good for brief outages and power fluctuations, with limited battery runtime.

1024Wh battery, 1800W AC output, advertised 10ms UPS transfer. Roughly 5–7 hours at a 120–150W printing load, accounting for conversion losses.

Best Buy

EcoFlow River 3 Plus 270 Portable Power Station, 268Wh LiFeP…

Compact alternative

268Wh battery, 600W continuous output and advertised 10ms UPS transfer. Roughly 1–1.7 hours at typical printing loads. Check availability.

How long will the printer run?

Assuming a 120V P1S printing at an average 150W:

Backup capacity

	

Approximate runtime

These are estimates for lithium power stations, not traditional lead-acid UPS units. Actual runtime depends on bed temperature, filament, inverter efficiency and battery condition.

One important correction to the initial sizing advice: Bambu's official specification is 350W maximum at 110V, versus 1000W at 220V. For a typical US outlet, a 600W unit can be sufficient, although additional headroom is useful.

Also, a power station's advertised UPS transfer time does not guarantee the P1S will stay running. Test the particular unit during a noncritical print.

Which should you buy?

For occasional flickers, I'd choose the CyberPower. For outages lasting an hour or longer, I'd choose a lithium power station with UPS functionality, such as the EcoFlow DELTA 3.

For a Bambu Lab P1S, I recommend a pure sine wave UPS rated at 1,000–1,500 VA, or a portable power station with a genuine UPS/EPS mode and sufficiently fast transfer time.

The key is preventing the printer from rebooting when power flickers. The P1S has power-loss recovery, but that doesn't guarantee a perfect print after an interruption.

What your P1S needs

Requirement

	

Recommendation




Printer power

	

Up to approximately 1,000 W on 110–120 V during bed heating




UPS output

	

1,000 W minimum for full-load coverage; 1,200 W+ preferred




Waveform

	

Pure sine wave




Transfer time

	

Ideally 10 ms or less; 0 ms with online UPS




Battery capacity

	

500–1,000 Wh for longer outages

The important distinction is that the P1S can draw much more power while heating its bed than during normal printing. A UPS that works while printing might overload when the printer starts heating.

One correction to the sizing above: on a US 110–120 V outlet, the P1S typically peaks around 350 W, not 1,000 W. The higher figure applies to 220–240 V operation. Normal printing is roughly 100–150 W.
